newsitem.title: USA: CSCE certified coffee stocks set new 12-year low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE certified coffee stocks set new 12-year low.

text.p: U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 750 60-kg bags in the week ended October 11, to set a fresh 12-year low of 29,974 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Monday.
The draw up occurred solely in the exchange's Miami warehouse, where stocks dropped to 519 bags.
The drawdown was well within expectations, traders said, although they noted there were no stocks pending exchange certification again this week.

Last week, the exchange-certified stockpile shrank to its lowest level in a decade, falling 945 bags to 30,724 bags. The continued downturn fueled persistant near-term supply concerns and buoyed prices to their highest settlement in six weeks on Friday.
Worries about tight spot supplies also bolstered the nearby December/March switch, which widened to 8.95 cents by the close Monday, up from 6.50 cents a week ago.
Spot December coffee fell 1.20 cents per lb on Monday, to finish at 115.10 cents, while second-month March ended 1.50 cents lower, at 106.15 cents.

Traders await the Green Coffee Association's September stock report after the close of business Tuesday. Green Coffee Association's consumer stocks could decline between 100,000 and 200,000 bags in September, traders said.
